name: Accessing Your Development Environment
apex: Explains how developers sign in depending on whether APEX runs in a local self-managed database or Oracle Cloud (Autonomous Database, Exadata, etc.).
workflow: Developer picks a sign-in path based on hosting; Cloud users go straight to a provisioned workspace URL.
relevance: Pure Oracle hosting/installation topology; Paddock Developer has one deployment (Cloudflare Worker) and no equivalent multi-hosting sign-in decision.
skip_for_web: Oracle Cloud/on-prem installation choice does not exist for a single-tenant Next.js app.

name: What Oracle APEX Is / How It Works
apex: APEX is a low-code platform that renders apps live from metadata stored in DB tables; browser-web server-database 3-tier architecture; no dedicated DB connection, session state managed server-side per request.
workflow: Developer edits metadata (pages/items/processes); APEX engine reads it and renders HTML on each request; no source code deploy step.
relevance: Paddock Developer already works this way: designer config renders storefront pages at request/build time; validates the metadata-driven page-composition model chosen for Paddock Developer.

name: Runtime vs Full Development Environment
apex: APEX installs as either a Runtime environment (run apps only, cannot modify) or Full Development environment (build, modify, run, delete apps).
workflow: Installer/DBA chooses the environment type at install time; production installs typically use Runtime only.
relevance: An install-time platform split with no Paddock analog; Paddock Developer is always full-edit for admins and read-only render for visitors, not a separate installable mode.
skip_for_web: No separate runtime-only install exists for a single Next.js deployment.

name: Workspace Home Page
apex: The first screen after sign-in; a dashboard of the workspace (a private virtual database/tenant) showing dev tools, activity, and announcements.
workflow: Developer signs in, lands here, then clicks a dev-tool card (usually App Builder) to go build; admins edit the Message/Resources regions to broadcast to the team.
relevance: Direct model for Paddock Developer's own landing/home page: a tool-launcher dashboard plus at-a-glance counts and an announcements strip, instead of dropping straight into a page list.

name: APEX Menu Bar
apex: A persistent left side-bar on almost every APEX page giving one-click access to the major tools, global search, and account controls.
workflow: Always visible; developer clicks an icon to jump tools without returning to a home page first.
relevance: Paddock Developer should keep a persistent nav rail (Pages, Components, Data, Settings) reachable from every designer screen rather than requiring a return to a dashboard each time.

name: Global Search (Spotlight Search)
apex: A universal search box in the menu bar that finds apps, pages, shared components, and utilities from anywhere, with typed-prefix syntax (e.g. 570:10) and scoped keyboard shortcuts.
attributes: scope shortcuts Ctrl+1 workspace/Ctrl+2 all apps/Ctrl+3 in-app/Ctrl+4 page
workflow: Developer presses the shortcut or clicks Search, types a name/ID, arrows to a result, and Enter jumps straight there.
relevance: Matches the operator's own note that Paddock's Page Finder needs search; APEX's scoped, keyboard-accelerated jump-to-page/component is the pattern to copy as a visible field, not a hidden command palette.

name: Extension Menu
apex: An optional menu bar item, populated only if a workspace admin added custom links (e.g. to community/support resources); hidden entirely when empty.
workflow: Admin adds links in Administration; then the menu appears between Search and Administration for everyone.
relevance: Thin admin-configured link list mainly for Oracle community resources (forums, blogs); Paddock has no equivalent ecosystem to link out to from designer chrome.
skip_for_web: Feature exists to point at Oracle's own community sites.

name: Administration Menu
apex: Menu bar item giving workspace admins access to Manage Service, Manage Users and Groups, Monitor Activity, Dashboards, and Change My Password.
workflow: Admin clicks the wrench icon to reach user/service management and usage dashboards without leaving the current page.
relevance: Confirms a distinct admin/ops menu (user management, activity monitoring) separate from page-building tools; worth checking Paddock Developer's Settings area surfaces usage/activity too, not just config.

name: Help Menu
apex: Menu bar item linking to Documentation, Discussion Forum, 'Learn More about Oracle APEX', and an About page with instance/version details.
attributes: About page (version, CGI env, DB info)
workflow: Developer clicks the question-mark icon to reach docs or diagnostic/version info.
relevance: A docs/version-info menu for a distributed product with a public forum; Paddock Developer is a private single-tenant tool with no community or version page to link to.
skip_for_web: No public docs/forum ecosystem for an internal designer.

name: Account Menu
apex: Menu bar item to edit your profile (email, name, photo, password), set preferences (default schema, date format, run-in-new-window), and switch Appearance (Automatic/Light/Dark), or sign out.
attributes: Preferences (default schema, date format, Unicode CSV, run in new window)
workflow: Developer clicks their account icon, opens Edit Profile or Preferences dialogs, applies changes, or signs out.
relevance: The three-way Appearance switch (Automatic/Light/Dark) is exactly the pattern for Paddock Developer's own dark-mode control; the DB-schema-default settings are Oracle-only.
skip_for_web: Default schema, date format and Unicode CSV settings are SQL Workshop specific with no Paddock equivalent.

name: App Builder (overview)
apex: The tool for creating and managing applications and pages; its home page lists installed apps, and selecting one opens that app's Application home page.
workflow: Developer opens App Builder from the Workspace home, sees all apps, clicks one to manage it.
relevance: Confirms the two-level drill-down (tool home to app list to one app's home) Paddock Developer should mirror: a Pages/Apps list screen before entering a single page's editor.

name: App Builder Home Page (access and first-run)
apex: Reached from the Workspace home; lists installed applications as a report, and in a brand-new workspace adds two extra call-to-action regions.
attributes: Create a New App region (new workspace only)
Install a Starter or Sample App region (new workspace only)
workflow: New workspace: developer picks Create a New App (wizard) or Install a Starter or Sample App (Gallery); established workspace: developer clicks an existing app card.
relevance: The empty-state pattern (two big CTAs: create new vs. install a starter) is exactly the first-run treatment Paddock Developer's App Builder home should show before any pages exist, instead of a bare empty list.

name: App Builder Home Page (regions and controls)
apex: The screen listing every installed application; top controls create/import/monitor apps, a center navigation bar searches and toggles the list view, and a side bar holds Recent apps and Task shortcuts.
workflow: Developer clicks Create for the wizard, uses search/view toggles to find an app, or uses sidebar Tasks (backups, export, facets, library app) and Recent list to jump back in.
relevance: Direct blueprint for Paddock Developer's Pages/Apps list screen: one primary Create action, secondary Import/Dashboard, list-or-icon view with search, plus a sidebar of Recent items and task shortcuts instead of a cluttered toolbar.

name: Library Application
apex: A special application that is a repository of reusable Shared Components (Authentication Schemes, Lists of Values, Text Messages, etc.); other apps subscribe to it via Component Groups to inherit centrally-defined components.
attributes: created from App Builder home Tasks list
workflow: Developer creates one Library Application per org, builds shared components in it, then other apps subscribe to inherit and stay in sync when it changes.
relevance: Matches Paddock's own Shared Components work (Lists, Component Settings); the missing piece worth copying is a formal subscribe-and-inherit mechanism across pages/sites rather than copy-paste reuse.

name: Application Home Page (controls)
apex: The per-app control center reached after picking an app in App Builder; run, edit definition, export, or browse and create its pages.
workflow: Developer clicks Run to preview, Create Page to add a page, or the page report/navigation bar to search and open existing pages for editing.
relevance: Best model for Paddock Developer's per-site home: one Run/Preview action, a clear Create Page action, a searchable page list with view toggle, and links out to Shared Components/Utilities/Export as siblings rather than buried menus.

name: Application Home Side Bar
apex: A right-hand sidebar of quick actions on the Application home page, separate from the main page list and toolbar.
attributes: Working Copy Tasks: Create Working Copy
workflow: Developer glances here for destructive/rare actions (delete, copy, lock) and a jump list of recently touched pages, without cluttering the main toolbar.
relevance: Worth copying for Paddock Developer's page-level home: keep rare or risky actions (delete, lock) visually separated from Create/Run, and surface a Recently Edited Pages list for quick resume.

name: Application Home Page Access Path
apex: Three-click path to the Application home page: sign in to the Workspace home, select App Builder, select an application.
workflow: Developer signs in once, then drills from Workspace to App Builder to a specific app each session.
relevance: Confirms the exact three-level navigation depth (workspace to builder to app) Paddock Developer's own information architecture should target: reach a page in three clicks from login.

name: Edit Profile Dialog
apex: Dialog to update your account: email, first/last name, profile photo, and password.
workflow: Developer opens Account menu, Edit Profile, edits fields, clicks Apply Changes.
relevance: Standard account-profile editing; Paddock already delegates this to Clerk's built-in profile UI, so there is nothing new here for Paddock Developer to design.
skip_for_web: Superseded by Clerk auth's own profile management already used in Paddock.

name: User Preferences and Appearance (Dark Mode)
apex: Account-menu dialog to toggle Appearance (Automatic/Light/Dark) and set developer preferences (default schema, date format, Unicode CSV, window/tab behavior for running apps).
attributes: Use single window to run all applications
workflow: Developer opens Account, Appearance to flip theme instantly, or Account, Preferences for SQL Workshop/runtime defaults, then Apply Changes.
relevance: The Automatic/Light/Dark three-state Appearance switch, applied instantly instance-wide, is the exact dark-mode control pattern for Paddock Developer's own settings; the schema/runtime-window prefs are Oracle/legacy-browser specific and not needed.
skip_for_web: Default schema, date format, Unicode CSV and popup-window prefs are SQL Workshop/legacy-browser specific with no Paddock use.

name: Oracle Help Center Documentation Access
apex: APEX links to a centrally hosted Oracle Help Center library (browsable by publication, searchable, downloadable as a ZIP); the Help menu can also be redirected at the instance level.
attributes: Books list to view all publications
workflow: Developer clicks Help, Documentation to reach the hosted manual set, or downloads it locally for offline reading.
relevance: A hosted multi-book documentation library is Oracle-product scale; Paddock Developer needs contextual in-app help, not a separate hosted doc site.
skip_for_web: No externally hosted multi-version documentation library exists or is needed for an internal single-tenant tool.

name: Field-Level Help and Page Designer Help
apex: Contextual (?) icons next to most fields open a tooltip/Help window on hover or click; Page Designer's Property Editor has a dedicated Help tab that updates live to describe whatever attribute is currently selected.
attributes: Help window with View Documentation link
Page Designer Help tab (live, per selected attribute)
Help menu: Getting Started in Page Designer
workflow: Developer hovers or clicks the (?) icon for a quick tip, or keeps the Property Editor's Help tab open while clicking through attributes to read live explanations.
relevance: Exactly the pattern Paddock Developer's settings/property panels should copy: a small inline help icon per field plus a persistent, selection-driven Help tab in the component editor, so non-technical admins never leave the page to understand a setting.

name: App Gallery
apex: A catalog of installable Sample Apps, Starter Apps, Utility Apps, and (if enabled) Custom Apps, each shown as a card with Install/Run/Edit/Remove actions and a More Info panel.
attributes: Utility Apps category (shown only if any exist)
Advanced Settings: Application ID / Parsing Schema
workflow: Developer opens Gallery from the menu bar or Global Search, browses cards by category, clicks Install (or Advanced Settings first), then later Run/Edit/Remove from the same card.
relevance: Maps directly to a starter-template gallery Paddock Developer should offer for new pages or sites: categorized cards, one-click install, and the same card growing Run/Edit/Remove actions once installed, cutting blank-canvas first-run friction.

name: Bookmarks and Rejoin Sessions
apex: Because APEX URLs normally embed a session ID, plain bookmarks break; developers enable support via a zero session ID (legacy) or the newer Rejoin Sessions feature, controllable at page, application, or instance level.
workflow: Developer enables Rejoin Sessions (or the legacy zero-session trick) on public pages so a saved or shared URL still works after the original session expires.
relevance: Solves a problem specific to APEX's stateful session-ID-in-URL architecture; Paddock's Next.js pages are already stateless and bookmarkable by default, so there is no equivalent gap to design for.
skip_for_web: Session-ID-in-URL is an APEX-only architecture quirk; standard web routing has no such problem.

name: Template Substitution Syntax
apex: Two syntaxes inject dynamic values into templates: placeholder #NAME# (component-scoped) and session-state &NAME. (page/app item reference), both resolved server-side before HTML is sent.
workflow: Developer writes a template with #COLUMN# or &ITEM. tokens; APEX substitutes the live value at render time.
relevance: Paddock Developer's component/template settings need an equivalent token syntax so a designer-authored template string can reference a page item or computed value without code; worth adopting a similar token convention.

name: Escape Filters (Output Escaping)
apex: Suffix filters (!ATTR, !HTML, !JS, !STRIPHTML, !RAW) applied to a substitution token control how its value is escaped before insertion, primarily to prevent XSS.
workflow: Developer appends the right filter to any token that renders user-supplied or dynamic content, choosing RAW only when the value is already trusted or sanitized.
relevance: Paddock Developer's page-composition engine needs the same explicit escaping contract wherever admin-entered or data-driven text is interpolated into HTML, so authors cannot accidentally open an XSS hole; RAW should stay opt-in, never default.

name: Built-in Substitution Strings, Legacy Text-Message Tokens, and JS Templates
apex: APEX ships many built-in substitution strings, a legacy APP_TEXT$Message_Name token for translated text messages, and a client-side apex.util.applyTemplate JS API to evaluate the same template syntax in the browser.
workflow: Developer looks up a built-in token for common values, or calls applyTemplate() client-side when building markup dynamically in JavaScript.
relevance: A large built-in-token library and a legacy translation-token format are APEX/PL-SQL-specific plumbing; Paddock's i18n and templating would use standard JS/React patterns instead.
skip_for_web: Legacy translation token format is explicitly deprecated by Oracle itself in favor of a newer syntax.

name: Theme Templates (Universal Theme, Theme Roller, Template Options)
apex: A theme is the full set of templates governing an app's layout and style; developers refine it further with Theme Styles (CSS on top of base CSS), Theme Roller (a live visual CSS editor for colors and corners), and per-component Template Options (declarative CSS modifier checkboxes).
workflow: Developer starts from the Universal Theme, tweaks colors live in Theme Roller, and picks per-component Template Options instead of hand-writing CSS.
relevance: Theme Roller's live visual color/style editing (no hand CSS) is a strong model for Paddock Developer's own site-wide styling controls, and Template Options mirrors the per-component Component Settings Paddock already ships.

name: Universal Theme Reference App
apex: A pre-built, installable reference application that documents the Universal Theme live: design foundations (colors, navigation, grid, page templates), a components catalog with examples, an icon catalog, and best-practice reference topics.
attributes: Design section (colors, navigation, grid layout, page templates, mobile patterns)
Components section (regions, lists, buttons with live examples)
Reference section (migrating, buttons, color, CSS variables, template directives)
workflow: Developer installs or opens the hosted reference app and browses live, working examples instead of reading static docs to learn the theme's components and conventions.
relevance: A living, running component-and-style catalog (like Storybook) is exactly what Paddock Developer should ship for its own component library, so admins see real interactive examples of every region/list/button type instead of a text list.

name: Viewing Session State (Developer Toolbar Session Page)
apex: A Developer Toolbar docked at the bottom of a running page; its Session, View Session State option opens a report of the current session's item values, with fields to jump to a page or search by item or collection name.
workflow: Developer runs the app, opens the toolbar's Session page, and inspects or searches live item values to debug why a condition or display is not behaving as expected.
relevance: The always-available bottom debug toolbar with a live state inspector is a good pattern for a Paddock Developer preview mode: an admin previewing a page could open a similar panel to see the page's resolved data and props.
skip_for_web: The session ID and workspace ID identifiers are APEX architecture-specific with no Paddock equivalent.

name: Session Overrides Dialog
apex: A developer-only runtime dialog to temporarily override, for your session only, the app's language, document direction, timezone, and internal file-path substitution strings (#APP_FILES#, #WORKSPACE_FILES#, #THEME_FILES#) or inject extra JS/CSS URLs.
workflow: Developer opens the dialog while testing, flips a language or timezone override to see the effect without changing the real app setting, then resets when done.
relevance: A per-developer runtime override of Oracle-specific virtual file-path variables; Paddock has no such indirection layer, though a lightweight preview-as locale/timezone QA toggle is a separate, smaller idea worth a mention.
skip_for_web: File-path substitution variables (#APP_FILES# etc.) are an APEX virtual-path mechanism with no Paddock analog.

name: f?p Legacy URL Syntax
apex: A legacy URL format (f?p=App:Page:Session:Request:Debug:ClearCache:itemNames:itemValues:PrinterFriendly) that encodes app ID, page number, session ID, and other runtime flags directly in the URL to link between pages.
workflow: Developer builds, or lets a wizard build, an f?p string to link a button or URL to a specific page while carrying session state and flags.
relevance: A legacy, Oracle-ORDS-specific URL scheme carrying a session ID and debug flags positionally; Paddock uses standard Next.js routes and query params, so nothing here transfers.
skip_for_web: Marked legacy by Oracle itself and tied to session-ID-bearing URLs, which Paddock's stateless routing does not use.

name: Hiding the Session ID on Public Pages
apex: Making a page Public (Authentication = Page is Public) and the app's Rejoin Sessions = Enabled for Public Sessions removes the session ID from that page's URL for anonymous visitors.
attributes: Application Definition: Security: Session Management: Rejoin Sessions Enabled for Public Sessions
Page: Rendering: Security: Authentication = Page is Public
workflow: Developer marks specific public pages' Authentication as Public and enables Rejoin Sessions at the app level so those URLs stay clean and shareable.
relevance: A fix for APEX's own session-ID-in-URL leakage; Paddock's URLs never carry a session ID so there is nothing to hide.
skip_for_web: Session-ID-in-URL does not exist in Paddock's routing model.

name: Referencing and Setting Session State
apex: Every page item's current value is auto-persisted as session state and can be read via SQL bind (:ITEM), PL/SQL (V('ITEM')), or static substitution (&ITEM.), and set via form submit, bind variable, computation, or URL.
attributes: Maintain Session State: Per Request (memory only)
Maintain Session State: Per User (disk, persists across sessions)
workflow: Developer reads an item's live value with the syntax matching the context (SQL/PL-SQL/template), and picks a Maintain Session State scope (memory/session/user) matching how long the value should persist.
relevance: The three-tier persistence scope (request-only, session, user-level-forever) is a useful model for Paddock Developer's own draft/form state: an in-memory preview edit versus a saved draft versus a persisted per-admin setting.
skip_for_web: The SQL/PL-SQL bind-variable syntax itself is Oracle Database specific.

name: Clearing Session State (Cache-Clear Codes)
apex: Special ClearCache tokens in f?p URLs reset item values to null at different scopes: a named item, a page, a report (RR full reset, CR filters only, RP pagination only), the whole app (APP), or the whole session (SESSION).
attributes: SESSION (APP scope across all apps in session)
workflow: Developer appends the right keyword to an f?p link's ClearCache segment so clicking it (e.g. New Order) starts from a guaranteed-blank form or report.
relevance: A positional-URL cache-reset vocabulary tied to APEX's stateful session model; a Next.js form simply resets local/React state or refetches, with no equivalent syntax needed.
skip_for_web: Entirely dependent on the f?p session-ID URL mechanism Paddock does not have.

name: Bind Variable Syntax in SQL/PL-SQL Regions
apex: Rules for referencing a page item as a SQL bind variable (:ITEM) inside a region's SQL query, LOV, or PL/SQL block: name must match an item, case-insensitive, max 30 characters, always VARCHAR2 requiring explicit conversion for dates/numbers.
workflow: Developer writes a WHERE clause or PL/SQL block referencing :ITEM_NAME directly; APEX substitutes the current session-state value as a real bind, reusing parsed SQL for performance.
relevance: Oracle SQL/PL-SQL bind-variable mechanics with a 30-character identifier limit; Paddock's data layer uses parameterized queries in TypeScript/Supabase with no such constraint.
skip_for_web: Oracle SQL identifier rules do not apply to Paddock's stack.

name: Session Cloning
apex: Opens a new browser tab with a distinct session ID that starts as a copy of the current session's values, using REQUEST=APEX_CLONE_SESSION, so multi-tab use does not corrupt shared state; logout in any cloned tab logs out all linked sessions.
workflow: Developer adds an open-in-new-tab link using the clone-session request value so users can safely multi-task without cross-tab state corruption.
relevance: Fixes a multi-tab problem caused by APEX's server-side shared session state; a Next.js app's per-request rendering and client-side React state do not share this failure mode across browser tabs.
skip_for_web: Multi-tab session corruption is specific to server-tracked session state, which Paddock's stateless request model does not have.

name: Output Escaping Defaults and Scope of Escape Filters
apex: APEX auto-escapes HTML/JS contexts by default; the !HTML/!ATTR/!JS/!RAW/!STRIPHTML filter suffixes give fine-grained override control across three token forms (&ITEM., interactive-grid column, #COLUMN# report column). The !JS filter only works in server-side substitution, not client-side.
attributes: applies to items, IG columns, and other report columns
workflow: Developer relies on APEX's automatic escaping by default and only appends an explicit filter when a specific context (e.g. inside an HTML attribute or a JS literal) needs different handling.
relevance: Confirms the right default for Paddock Developer's own templating: auto-escape everything by default, and require an explicit, visible opt-out (like !RAW) rather than ever defaulting to unescaped output.

name: Substitution Strings Report (per Template)
apex: Each template definition includes a Substitution Strings report listing exactly which #TOKEN# placeholders that specific template supports, found under Shared Components, Templates.
workflow: Developer opens a template and checks its Substitution Strings report to see which tokens are valid before writing markup that references them.
relevance: A per-template list of valid tokens, discoverable in the editor itself, is a good small feature for Paddock Developer's component/template editor so authors do not guess or grep source for available placeholders.

name: Team Development (Overview, Setup, Toolbar)
apex: Oracle's built-in per-workspace issue tracker for the dev team; setup installs sample labels, templates and milestones, and a toolbar on every Team Dev page offers Notifications, Jump-to links, and New Issue.
attributes: Accessing Team Development (Workspace home or Workspace Utilities)
workflow: Dev team completes one-time setup, then uses the toolbar's Jump to and New Issue to work issues without leaving Team Development.
relevance: A bundled bug tracker for the development team building the app, unrelated to composing content pages; Paddock's own dev workflow already uses GitHub Issues, and Paddock Developer's users are content admins, not engineers.
skip_for_web: Duplicate of GitHub Issues, which Paddock already uses for its own engineering workflow.

name: Creating and Updating Issues (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents topic pointing to the Issues page, issue creation, bulk update, and single-issue update sub-pages.
relevance: Stub page for the issue-tracker sub-topics; no new concept beyond what its child pages cover.

name: Issues Page
apex: The Team Development issue-tracker home: a searchable Cards-or-Grid list of issues with bulk Update actions (status, assignees, labels, milestones) and Open Issues / Feedback summary counters in the sidebar.
attributes: Issue card: title, status icon, owner, labels, assignee, comment count
workflow: Developer scans cards or switches to grid, multi-selects issues, and bulk-applies a status, label or milestone via the Update menu.
relevance: The bug tracker's own list screen, not a page-building tool; its Cards/Grid toggle and summary-counter sidebar are generic list-UI patterns already captured from the App Builder home page notes.
skip_for_web: Issue-tracking screen with no content-authoring purpose for Paddock Developer.

name: Creating an Issue (New Issue Dialog)
apex: Dialog to log a new issue: pick a starter Template (or none), enter a Title and Markdown Issue Text, preview the rendered HTML, then Create Issue.
attributes: Template picker (or Continue without a template)
workflow: Developer clicks New Issue, optionally starts from a template, writes a Markdown description, previews it, and submits.
relevance: Standard bug-report form for the bundled tracker; Paddock has no in-app issue tracker to replicate, though the Markdown-editor-with-live-preview pattern is already common in Paddock's own content editing.

name: Updating Multiple Issues at Once
apex: Bulk-edit flow: check multiple issues on the Issues page, then use the Update menu to mass-apply a Status, Assignees, Labels, or Milestones change, confirmed with Apply Changes.
workflow: Developer multi-selects issues, opens one Update sub-menu, toggles Assign/Remove per value, and applies once for the whole selection.
relevance: A bulk-edit pattern for the bug tracker's own records; if Paddock Developer ever needs bulk-tag or bulk-status editing across content pages, this checkbox-select-then-mass-apply shape is reusable, but the fields themselves are tracker-only.

name: Updating an Issue (overview and ownership rule)
apex: Table-of-contents topic for editing an issue, noting only the issue owner or an administrator may change its title, description, or delete it.
attributes: Associating an Issue with an App and Page
relevance: Stub page for the issue-tracker edit sub-topics; the owner-or-admin-only edit rule is a reasonable general permission pattern but not a new concept Paddock lacks.

name: Issue Details Page
apex: An issue's full record: a reverse-chronological Issue Timeline of events (edits, comments) below the Issue Text, an Add Comment box with templates and preview, and an Actions menu for every state change; Notifications subscribes to updates and Attachments lists files.
attributes: Add Comment (formatting tools, Response Template, Preview)
Actions menu (Edit Title/Text, Set Assignees/Labels/Milestones, Associate App or Page, Mark Duplicate, Delete, Close)
workflow: Developer opens an issue, reads the timeline top-down, adds a comment (optionally from a template) or picks an Actions item to change state, and subscribes to be notified of further events.
relevance: The reverse-chronological event timeline plus threaded comments plus a Subscribe toggle is a strong pattern for a Paddock Developer content-item history view (who changed what and when on a page), separate from the tracker-specific fields.

name: Updating the Issue Title
apex: Owner/admin-only inline edit: Actions menu, Edit Title opens a one-field dialog, Apply Changes saves.
workflow: Developer opens Actions, Edit Title, retypes the title, applies.
relevance: Trivial single-field rename dialog; no new pattern beyond standard inline editing already assumed in Paddock Developer.

name: Updating the Issue Description (Issue Text)
apex: Owner/admin-only edit of the issue body via a Markdown editor with a Preview step before Apply Changes.
workflow: Developer opens Edit Issue Text, writes Markdown, previews the rendered HTML, applies.
relevance: Same Markdown-edit-then-preview pattern already noted for issue creation; nothing new for Paddock Developer.

name: Setting Assignees
apex: Actions menu, Set Assignees opens a multi-select dialog of workspace users; applying logs a timeline event and lists assignees in the sidebar.
workflow: Developer opens Set Assignees, checks one or more users, applies; the sidebar and timeline update immediately.
relevance: Tracker-specific people-assignment; Paddock Developer has no per-page assignee concept, though instantly updating both sidebar and timeline on any change is a good micro-pattern for feedback.

name: Setting Labels (on an Issue)
apex: Same Actions-menu multi-select dialog pattern as Assignees, applied to Labels; identical Apply Changes and timeline-logging mechanics.
workflow: Developer opens Set Labels, checks or unchecks labels, applies.
relevance: Same mechanic as Setting Assignees; the underlying Labels concept itself is covered separately under Managing Labels.

name: Setting Milestones (on an Issue), with Date-Colored Status
apex: Same Actions-menu multi-select pattern as Labels/Assignees, plus each assigned milestone shows red, yellow, or green depending on how close its date is (past, within 2 weeks, or further out).
attributes: milestone color: green (more than 2 weeks out)
workflow: Developer assigns one or more milestones; each renders color-coded by urgency so overdue ones stand out at a glance.
relevance: The red/yellow/green urgency-by-date coloring is a small but useful pattern wherever a date matters in Paddock Developer (a scheduled publish date, an upcoming race weekend) for instant visual urgency without reading the date.

name: Associating an Issue with an App and Page
apex: Actions menu dialog to link an issue to a specific application and page plus a free-text comment, so a bug report points straight at the screen it affects.
attributes: Actions menu: Associate with App and Page
workflow: Developer opens the dialog, picks the app and page the issue is about, adds a note, applies; a timeline event records it.
relevance: Cross-links a bug report to a page for the dev team's own tracker; Paddock Developer's own content items do not need to reference themselves this way.

name: Marking an Issue as Duplicate
apex: Actions menu dialog to pick another issue as the original; a distinct two-green-pages icon marks the duplicate event in the timeline.
workflow: Developer selects the original issue from a picker and applies; the timeline logs the link with a unique icon.
relevance: Bug-tracker deduplication has no analog in a content-page designer.

name: Closing and Reopening an Issue
apex: A single Actions-menu toggle (Close Issue / Reopen Issue) flips status; the status icon switches green-to-red (or back) and a plain-language timeline event records the change.
attributes: status icon: green (open) vs red with check (closed)
timeline event: set status for this issue to CLOSED/OPEN Now
workflow: Developer clicks Close Issue when resolved, or finds a closed issue and clicks Reopen Issue if it recurs.
relevance: Standard open/closed toggle already implicit wherever Paddock has a status field; the icon-color-plus-plain-language-timeline-line combo is a nice small touch worth keeping in mind generally.

name: Managing Deleted Issues (Soft Delete, Reinstate, Purge)
apex: Three-stage deletion safety net: owner or admin deletes an issue (soft delete) with a confirmation step, a Manage Deleted Issues page lets it be reinstated, and a separate Permanently Delete Selected or Purge All step is needed to actually erase it.
workflow: Developer deletes an issue (recoverable), later either reinstates it from Manage Deleted Issues or, once certain, permanently deletes it individually or purges everything.
relevance: Exactly the soft-delete-then-recoverable-then-purge pattern Paddock Developer's own Delete Page needs (flagged as important in the operator's Page Designer walkthrough notes) instead of one irreversible delete button.

name: Viewing Your User Profile (My Issues and Notifications)
apex: A personal profile view reached via the toolbar's Notifications icon: an Issues tab listing everything you own or watch, and a Notifications tab logging every event on those issues with a Clear Notifications action and a link to Notification Preferences.
workflow: Developer clicks the toolbar's Notifications icon to see a personal feed of events on issues they own or watch, or switches to the Issues tab to see just the list.
relevance: A generic my-stuff profile plus notification feed; a reasonable shape in the abstract but nothing APEX-specific for Paddock Developer to copy beyond patterns already common in web apps.

name: Managing Labels (Label Groups, Exclusive vs Non-Exclusive)
apex: A two-level tagging system: Label Groups (named, color-coded, and either Exclusive, only one label from the group at a time, or Non-Exclusive, many at once) each containing individual Labels, edited via an editable interactive grid.
attributes: editable interactive grid (bulk cell edit, multi-row delete)
workflow: Developer creates a color-coded group, decides if it is exclusive (like a single status) or not (like multiple feature tags), then adds or edits labels in a spreadsheet-like grid.
relevance: The exclusive-vs-non-exclusive group distinction (a mutually exclusive status tag versus freely combinable tags) is a useful taxonomy model for any Paddock Developer tagging feature, plus color-coding per group for quick visual scanning.

name: Managing Milestones (Create, Edit, Delete)
apex: A dated tracking marker with a Name, URL Slug, Date, Open/Closed Status, and Description; edited or deleted from a Milestones list with a delete confirmation dialog.
workflow: Developer creates a milestone with a target date, assigns issues to it elsewhere, and later marks it Closed or deletes it once passed.
relevance: A generic dated-marker CRUD form; Paddock's own dated concepts (race weekends, publish schedules) already exist as first-class data, not something to model after a bug tracker's milestone feature.

name: Managing Templates (Issue and Response Starter Text)
apex: Reusable starter-text snippets of two types (Issue or Response) with Name, Description, and Markdown body, selectable when creating an issue or writing a comment.
workflow: Developer authors a template once, then anyone creating an issue or comment picks it from a list to prefill starter text instead of typing from scratch.
relevance: The reusable, typed (Issue vs Response) starter-text-snippet picker is a good small pattern for Paddock Developer's own content authoring: canned block or section templates by type that content editors pick from.

name: Using Team Development Utilities (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents topic for the admin-only Utilities page covering deleted-issue management, templates, milestones, labels, uploaded files, data purge, bulk reassignment, and notification preferences.
attributes: Removing a Milestone for All Issues
relevance: Stub page; the individual admin utilities it lists are assessed on their own pages.

name: Team Development Utilities Page (Admin Hub)
apex: A flat admin-only link list aggregating every maintenance operation for the tracker: deleted-issue management, templates, milestones, labels, uploaded files, data purge, bulk reassignment, and notification-preference management for all workspace users.
workflow: Admin opens Jump to, Utilities to reach any bulk or maintenance operation from one hub instead of hunting through individual issue screens.
relevance: Confirms the value of a single admin-only utilities hub for bulk and maintenance operations, separate from everyday content editing; Paddock Developer's Settings area should keep the same one-stop-shop shape for admin-only bulk actions.

name: Managing Uploaded Files (Issues Files Report)
apex: A flat report of every file attached to any issue in the workspace (file name, issue, size, date, user), with links to download or jump to the parent issue, and admin-only bulk delete.
attributes: Issues Files report (name, issue, size, date, user)
workflow: Admin browses all attachments workspace-wide in one report instead of opening each issue, and bulk-deletes stale ones.
relevance: A cross-record attachment index for the bug tracker; if Paddock Developer ever manages uploaded media across pages, a flat all-files-with-back-link report is the reusable idea, but the tracker specifics are not.

name: Purging Data (Admin, by Component)
apex: Admin-only page to permanently wipe all data for selected Team Development components (issues, labels, etc.) in one irreversible Delete action, with a text warning.
workflow: Admin selects which components to wipe and confirms; there is no further undo.
relevance: An irreversible bulk-wipe backed only by a text warning is a weaker safety pattern than Paddock's own house rule of pasting exactly what will be lost and getting explicit approval; nothing to copy, and something to avoid.

name: Reassigning Issues to Another Assignee (Bulk, Admin)
apex: Admin picks a From assignee and a To assignee, optionally restricted to Open issues only, previews the affected issue list, then confirms Change Assignee.
workflow: Admin picks old and new assignee, reviews the generated list of affected issues before committing, then confirms.
relevance: The From/To bulk-reassign with a mandatory preview-before-confirm step is a solid safety pattern for any Paddock Developer bulk operation (e.g. reassigning ownership across many pages): show what will change before it changes.

name: Reassigning the Issue Owner (Bulk, Admin)
apex: Same From/To bulk-reassignment-with-preview mechanic as reassigning an assignee, applied to the Issue Owner field instead.
workflow: Admin picks old and new owner, reviews the affected issue list, confirms.
relevance: Identical mechanic to Reassigning Issues to Another Assignee, already credited there; no new pattern.

name: Removing a Milestone for All Issues (Bulk, Admin)
apex: Admin picks a milestone (optionally Open issues only), previews affected issues, then confirms Remove Milestone.
workflow: Admin selects the milestone to strip workspace-wide, reviews the preview, confirms.
relevance: Same preview-before-bulk-change mechanic already credited under Reassigning Issues to Another Assignee; no new pattern.

name: Removing Labels for All Issues (Bulk, Admin)
apex: Admin picks a Label or Label Group (optionally Open issues only), previews affected issues, then confirms Remove Labels.
workflow: Admin selects the label to strip workspace-wide, reviews the preview, confirms.
relevance: Same preview-before-bulk-change mechanic already credited; no new pattern.

name: Managing Notification Preferences (Self and Admin-for-Others)
apex: Per-user settings for whether to receive emails, at what Frequency (Immediately, Hourly Summary, Daily Summary), and which event types trigger a notification; admins can add or edit these settings for any workspace user.
workflow: User sets their own email/frequency/event preferences; an admin can additionally provision or override another user's preferences from the same form.
relevance: A full per-user notification-preferences system for a multi-developer team; Paddock is a two-person team with no comparable notification-fatigue problem to solve yet.

name: Feedback Feature (End-User Widget)
apex: An optional app Feature that adds a Feedback icon to the running application's nav bar; visitors rate their experience with an emoji (Positive/Neutral/Negative), write a comment, and optionally attach a file.
attributes: Feature: Feedback (added via Create Application/Page Wizard)
workflow: A site visitor clicks the Feedback icon anywhere in the app, rates their experience, types a comment, optionally attaches a file, and submits; the entry captures the app name, page, timestamp, and user info automatically.
relevance: A lightweight, always-available emoji-rating-plus-comment feedback widget is directly useful for Paddock's own site (a tell-us-whats-wrong-on-this-page control), and Paddock Developer could offer it as an installable Feature the same way APEX does.

name: Reviewing and Tracking Feedback (Admin Triage)
apex: Admins triage feedback per-application (Administration, User Feedback) or workspace-wide (Team Development Feedback dashboard/report/by-filer/calendar), classifying each entry by Type, Disposition, and Status, with one click to spin an entry into a tracked issue.
workflow: Admin opens the dashboard, drills into a specific feedback entry, classifies its Type, Disposition and Status, optionally converts it into a tracked issue, and applies.
relevance: The dashboard-plus-triage-queue with a Type/Disposition/Status pipeline is a strong model for a Paddock Developer feedback inbox: visitor-submitted notes classified and optionally promoted into real follow-up work, instead of getting lost in email.

name: Tracking Feedback (Dashboard, Report, By Filer, Calendar)
apex: Four workspace-wide views of the same feedback log: a Dashboard of counts (open feedback, users, entries) linking into filtered lists, a filterable Report for full triage, a By Filing User breakdown, and a Calendar view by date.
attributes: dashboard breakdowns: By Status/By Application/By Filer
workflow: Admin starts at the Dashboard for an at-a-glance count, then drills into the Report to triage individual entries or the Calendar to see feedback volume over time.
relevance: Elaborates the same admin triage screen already credited as relevant under Managing Feedback; the extra views here (By Filer, Calendar) are minor variants of one underlying feedback log, not a distinct new pattern.

name: Application Types (Standard, Theme, Library, Boilerplate)
apex: Four application kinds set on the Application Definition: Standard (default, general apps), Theme (holds a visual theme's styles/templates), Library (holds reusable shared components other apps subscribe to), Boilerplate (seeded subscriptions plus pre-built pages to jump-start a new app).
attributes: set via Application Definition: Properties: Application Type
workflow: Developer usually leaves an app as Standard; picks Theme or Library only when building a shared asset for other apps to subscribe to, or Boilerplate to seed a new app fast.
relevance: The Library/Theme app-as-shared-asset idea plus Boilerplate (a pre-populated starting point) both map to features Paddock Developer should offer: a start-from-a-template-site option and a formal shared-component source, distinct from a normal content page.

name: Create an Application (Method Picker)
apex: The landing screen after clicking Create on the App Builder home page, offering five ways to start a new app: one-click Create Application (simple), the full Create App Wizard, Generative AI prompt, From a File (CSV/XLSX/XML/JSON), or Fusion Integration.
attributes: Create App Using Generative AI (if configured)
workflow: Developer clicks Create, is presented with these five method cards, and picks based on how much structure they already have: nothing, a data source, a file, or natural language.
relevance: The multi-path how-do-you-want-to-start fork (blank/wizard/AI-prompt/import-a-file) is exactly the decision Paddock Developer's own New Page or New Site flow should offer up front, rather than always dropping into one fixed wizard.

name: Simple Create Application Wizard
apex: The fastest app-creation path: enter just a Name and click Create Application; produces a minimal app of a Global Page, Home page, and Login page, with everything else added later via the Create Page Wizard.
workflow: Developer names the app, clicks once, lands on a working three-page skeleton, then adds real pages one at a time afterward.
relevance: The one-field, one-click give-it-a-name-and-get-a-skeleton path is the right default for Paddock Developer's own New Page or New Site flow when the admin has no data model yet and just wants to start.

name: Full Create Application Wizard (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents topic for the full, multi-page Create Application Wizard: how it works, how to run it, and its Page Types, Features, and Settings.
attributes: About the Full Create Application Wizard
Running the Full Create Application Wizard
Understanding Page Types, Features, and Settings
relevance: Stub page; its child topics carry the actual content and are assessed separately.

name: Full Create Application Wizard (What It Builds)
apex: The wizard's four-part flow: Name and Appearance, then add Pages (calendars, cards, charts, dashboards, forms, interactive grids, master-detail/editable grids, reports), then one-time application-level Features, then generation Settings; every run also saves a reusable Application Blueprint (JSON).
workflow: Developer works top to bottom through Name/Appearance, Pages, Features, Settings, then generates; the resulting blueprint can be reused to add more pages or edited as JSON.
relevance: This four-stage shape (identity/appearance, then content pages, then one-time app-level features, then technical settings) is the right structure for Paddock Developer's own New Site wizard, ending in a reusable, editable blueprint rather than a one-shot throwaway wizard.

name: Create Application Wizard: Icon, Name, Appearance
apex: First wizard step: pick an app icon (upload or a color-coded icon library, reused as favicon, PWA icon, Apple touch icon, and App Builder icon), name the app, and set Appearance (Theme Style plus a Navigation type: Side Menu, Top Menu, or Mega Menu).
workflow: Developer picks an icon and name, then opens Appearance to choose a theme style and one of three navigation shapes before adding any pages.
relevance: One icon reused everywhere (favicon, PWA, app-list thumbnail) and a navigation-shape choice made once up front are patterns Paddock Developer's New Site setup should copy, instead of configuring icons and nav separately per surface.

name: Create Application Wizard: Adding and Managing Pages
apex: Click Add Page and pick a page type to add it to the app's page list; reorder pages by drag handle (Home page always first), or Edit a page's attributes, or Delete it, all before generating.
workflow: Developer adds one or more pages by type, drags to set the order the admin or nav will follow, and edits or removes any page before clicking Create Application.
relevance: Add-by-type plus drag-to-reorder plus edit-in-place is exactly the page-list interaction Paddock Developer needs when assembling a new site's page tree during setup, not just after the fact.

name: Create Application Wizard: Features Step
apex: A checklist of one-time, application-level Features to include (e.g. PWA install, Push Notifications, About Page, Access Control, Activity Reporting, Configuration Options, Feedback, Theme Style Selection); a Check All shortcut selects everything, and each has field-level Help.
workflow: Developer scans the checklist and ticks whichever app-wide capabilities the new app needs; unticked features can still be added later one at a time via the Create Page Wizard's Feature pages.
relevance: A checklist of optional, app-wide capabilities decided once at setup, not per-page, is the right shape for Paddock Developer's New Site setup: PWA, feedback widget, access control, etc. as opt-in checkboxes with inline help.

name: Create Application Wizard: Settings Step
apex: Generation-time configuration: Application ID (auto-generated, 3000-9000 reserved for Oracle), Schema (DB schema whose privileges the app runs as), Authentication method, Languages (primary plus additional), Advanced Settings (definition, preference, security and globalization attributes), and UI Defaults.
workflow: Developer accepts the generated Application ID, picks the schema and authentication method, sets the primary language, and optionally opens Advanced Settings or UI Defaults before generating.
relevance: The generation-time settings block (identity/ID, security boundary, auth method, language, advanced/UI defaults) maps to what Paddock Developer's New Site setup needs to decide once: a slug/ID, an access mode, a default locale, kept behind an Advanced disclosure.
skip_for_web: The Schema field specifically, an Oracle DB privilege boundary, has no Paddock equivalent since Paddock's data access model does not vary per site.

name: Available Page Types (Create Application Wizard)
apex: The catalog of page types the wizard can add, from a blank canvas to fully-featured data pages: Blank, Calendar, Cards, Chart, Dashboard, Faceted Search, Smart Filters, Form, Interactive Grid, Interactive Report, Map, Master Detail, and Additional Pages (Classic Report, Multiple Reports, Timeline, Wizard).
workflow: Developer picks a page type per page while adding pages in the wizard (or later via Create Page Wizard); each type drives a different follow-up UI (choose a table, chart type, layout, etc.).
relevance: A fixed catalog of page archetypes, each with its own guided setup, is exactly the model for Paddock Developer's own New Page type picker instead of one generic blank-region page for everything.

name: Cards Page Type
apex: A page of information tiles in Grid, Float, or Horizontal (Row) layout, fully customizable (layout, icon, badge, media) with declarative click actions (Button, Full Card, Title, Subtitle, or Media) and template-directive conditional formatting.
workflow: Developer points a Cards page at a data source, picks a layout, and decides what clicking each part of a card (the whole card, just the title, the media) should do.
relevance: Directly matches Paddock's own driver/team/race card grids; the three named layouts and the per-card-zone click-action model (title vs media vs whole card) is worth adopting explicitly in Paddock Developer's Cards component settings.

name: Faceted Search Page Type
apex: An ecommerce-style search layout: a left-hand facet region to narrow results (each facet showing possible values plus an occurrence count) beside a report region, with built-in search, optional per-facet chart (bar or pie), and facet groups for multi-flag-column data models.
workflow: Developer builds a report, then exposes chosen columns as facets so visitors narrow results by clicking values instead of writing a query.
relevance: The occurrence-count-per-facet-value ecommerce pattern is exactly right for browsing Paddock's results/standings by season, series, team, or driver; strongly worth a dedicated Faceted Search component in Paddock Developer.

name: Smart Filters Page Type
apex: A more space-efficient alternative to Faceted Search: one search field at top showing filters as suggestion chips; clicking a chip applies it (moving it to an Applied Filters area) and results render as a classic report, cards, map, or calendar.
attributes: clicking a filter name opens a value list
workflow: Visitor types or clicks a suggested filter chip, it moves to Applied Filters, and the chosen result view (cards, map, etc.) updates.
relevance: A chip-based filter bar that renders into cards or a map is a strong, more compact alternative to full faceted search for Paddock's smaller filter sets (e.g. a single season's races), worth offering as a second filter-UI option.

name: Interactive Grid and Interactive Report Page Types
apex: Power-user report pages with extensive end-user customization (sort, filter, group by, pivot, control break, aggregates, saved private/alternative reports, CSV/HTML/PDF/Excel download); Interactive Grid additionally supports inline spreadsheet-style editing and drag rearrangement.
workflow: Developer builds the base report; end users then reshape it themselves each session (or save their arrangement) without any developer involvement.
relevance: Deep spreadsheet-grade, end-user-customizable reporting (pivot, saved personal report variants) is built for internal data-entry/analysis apps; Paddock's public content pages need curated, developer-controlled views, not visitor-configurable pivot tables.
skip_for_web: Visitor-side pivot/group-by/saved-personal-reports has no place on a public content site; an admin data-review screen might want a lighter version of sort/filter/export only.

name: Map Page Type
apex: A background map plus spatial layers (Points, Lines, Polygons, Heat Map, or Extruded Polygons) sourced from a geometry column (SDO_GEOMETRY/VARCHAR2/CLOB with GeoJSON) or two numeric lat/long columns.
workflow: Developer points a Map page at a table with either a geometry column or lat/long columns and picks which layer type to render.
relevance: A ready-made map component (points/lines/polygons from simple lat/long columns) is directly useful for Paddock: circuit locations, a season's calendar plotted on a map, or a live-timing track layout.

name: Master Detail Page Type
apex: A one-to-many editing pattern across two tables in three layouts: Stacked (one page, editable grids, pick a master row to see details), Side by Side (master list left, selected record plus details right, modal edit), or Drill Down (two pages: master report, then a form-plus-detail-grids page).
workflow: Developer picks a layout based on how much screen space and how many detail rows are typical, then wires it to the master and detail tables.
relevance: A relational data-entry pattern (insert/update/delete across parent and child tables); Paddock's content relationships (e.g. a race and its results) are populated by data pipelines, not by an admin editing master-detail grids by hand.
skip_for_web: No admin CRUD screen in Paddock currently edits parent/child records this way.

name: Feature: Install Progressive Web App
apex: Adds an Install App navigation-bar entry and lets users install the app on their device as a Progressive Web App.
workflow: Developer checks the Feature at app creation; users then see and can click Install App.
relevance: Paddock already ships as a PWA via @serwist/next; this confirms opt-in PWA install prompting as a standard app-level feature, matching what Paddock already has.

name: Feature: Push Notifications
apex: Adds a User Settings nav-bar entry letting visitors subscribe or unsubscribe to web push notifications sent even when they are not on the site.
workflow: Developer enables the feature once; visitors then opt in via User Settings and receive pushes triggered by the app.
relevance: Push notifications for race-weekend alerts or new content would be a natural Paddock feature; APEX's opt-in-checkbox-plus-User-Settings-entry pattern is a clean model to copy if Paddock adds this.

name: Feature: About Page
apex: Adds a simple About page displaying the application's description, reached from a help icon in the navigation bar.
attributes: reached via nav bar help icon
workflow: Developer writes a Description in Settings; the feature just wires up a page and a nav link to display it.
relevance: A generic static About page; Paddock already has its own about and information content pages, not something the designer needs to special-case as an installable feature.

name: Feature: Access Control (Roles)
apex: Adds role-based authorization with three built-in roles (Administrator, Contributor, Reader) that can each be granted different access to pages, menu entries, regions, columns, items, and buttons.
workflow: Developer enables the feature, then assigns each role's allowed access down to individual page components.
relevance: A built-in three-tier role model usable down to individual buttons and columns is a strong, ready-made permission scheme for Paddock Developer's own multi-admin access control, rather than inventing roles from scratch.

name: Feature: Activity Reporting
apex: Adds a bundle of built-in usage reports: Top Users, Application Error Log, Page Performance, Application activity by page, Page Views detail, and an Automations Log.
workflow: Developer checks the feature once; the reports appear ready-made under Utilities with no separate build step.
relevance: A one-click bundle of usage, error, and performance reports added once at app creation is a good model for Paddock Developer's own analytics: ship a standard reporting pack instead of building each report ad hoc.

name: Feature: Configuration Options
apex: Lets administrators toggle specific pieces of app functionality on or off at runtime via admin-defined build options, without a code change.
workflow: Developer wires a build option to a chunk of functionality; an admin later flips it on or off from a settings screen with no redeploy.
relevance: Runtime feature flags exposed to admins, not just developers, is valuable for Paddock Developer: let a content admin enable or disable an experimental module themselves, echoing Paddock's own GrowthBook-style flag concept.

name: Feature: Feedback (Wizard Checkbox)
apex: The same Feedback widget covered under Team Development, offered here as a one-time opt-in checkbox at app creation instead of added later via the Create Page Wizard.
workflow: Developer ticks Feedback while running the Create Application Wizard instead of adding it as a separate page afterward.
relevance: Already assessed as relevant under Team Development's Feedback Feature; this entry is just the same feature's app-creation checkbox, not new.

name: Feature: Theme Style Selection (End-User Choice)
apex: Lets administrators expose a Customize link on the home page so end users can pick their own color-scheme theme style (e.g. a higher-contrast Iris style), separate from the developer's own Theme Roller.
attributes: Allow End Users to choose Theme Style toggle
workflow: Developer enables the toggle; visitors then click Customize on the home page and pick from the available styles.
relevance: End-user-selectable color themes framed explicitly around accessibility, a higher-contrast option, is worth adding to Paddock's own appearance settings alongside dark mode.

name: Advanced Settings (Application Definition Detail)
apex: Grouped app-creation-time settings, editable later too: UI Defaults/Copy-from-Existing-Apps/Table Prefixes, a Short Description and Description (home page and About page), Settings (footer branding, Version, Logging, Debugging), Security (Deep Linking, max session length, max idle time), and Globalization (document direction, date/time/timestamp formats).
attributes: Add Built with APEX to Footer
workflow: Developer sets these once at creation but can revisit anytime; most stay default except Deep Linking, session limits, and Logging when hardening for production.
relevance: The security trio (deep-linking toggle, max session length, max idle time) and the on/off activity Logging switch are useful app-level settings Paddock Developer should expose per site or page-tree, not only as global env config.
skip_for_web: Table Prefixes and Copy from Existing Apps are Oracle schema/table-generation conveniences with no Paddock equivalent, since Paddock does not generate DB tables from a wizard.

name: Removing Wizard-Added Features via Build Options
apex: Every wizard-added Feature is wired to a Build Option; setting that option to Exclude makes APEX treat the feature and its components as if absent, and deleting the option (after removing its components) removes the feature permanently.
attributes: permanent removal: delete components then delete the build option
workflow: Developer flips a feature's build option to Exclude to soft-disable it for testing, or fully removes it by deleting its components then the option itself.
relevance: A soft-disable-via-flag-before-hard-delete pattern for whole features, not just content, is a good safety net for Paddock Developer: let an admin toggle a feature off before any destructive removal.

name: Creating an App Using Generative AI (APEX Assistant Chat)
apex: A conversational app-creation flow: the APEX Assistant chat asks for a natural-language description (including which tables to use), proposes a summary of the app and pages it will build, accepts follow-up messages to refine the plan, and only then opens the full Create Application Wizard pre-filled for final review.
attributes: requires a Generative AI Service with Used by App Builder enabled
Create Application hands off to the full wizard, pre-filled
workflow: Developer describes the desired app in plain language, reviews the AI's proposed summary, refines with more messages if needed, then reviews and edits the pre-filled wizard before finalizing.
relevance: This chat-then-review-then-confirm flow (describe in prose, get a proposed structure, refine conversationally, land in a normal editable form) is precisely the shape Paddock Developer should use for an AI-assisted describe-the-page-you-want entry point, given Claude already powers this agent.

name: Spec-Driven Development (SDD) via APEX Blueprints
apex: A three-phase AI workflow: feed an AI coding agent a functional specification, database schema metadata, and a system prompt; it produces a human-readable Markdown blueprint describing every page, region, report, form, chart, filter, and action; the developer reviews that blueprint before importing it, and APEX builds a baseline app from it.
attributes: Input: schema metadata (via Describe Tables utility)
Import step (maps each blueprint section to a component)
workflow: Developer or their AI agent writes a spec, exports schema metadata, generates a blueprint, reviews the readable Markdown before committing, then imports it to scaffold a real baseline app.
relevance: An inspectable, human-readable intermediate artifact between a natural-language spec and generated components is the exact safety valve Paddock Developer needs for AI-assisted page generation: let the admin read and edit the plan before anything is actually created.

name: Boilerplate Applications (Create and Use)
apex: A boilerplate app is a fully-editable existing app repurposed as a starting point; setting Application Type to Boilerplate marks it, and Create App From a Boilerplate clones it into a new, independent app (naming it, optionally changing its ID/parsing schema, optionally copying Supporting Object Definitions) while keeping its references to Library and Theme apps intact.
attributes: mark existing app: Application Type = Boilerplate
Create App From a Boilerplate wizard
new app is independent after creation, but keeps Library/Theme subscriptions
workflow: Developer builds one well-configured app, flips it to Boilerplate, and every future similar app starts as a full independent copy of it instead of from scratch, while still inheriting the shared Library/Theme.
relevance: The clone-a-known-good-app-as-a-starting-point-then-go-independent-but-keep-shared-subscriptions pattern is exactly what Paddock Developer needs for a duplicate-this-page-or-site-as-a-new-template feature.

name: Creating an Application from a File (Load Data Wizard)
apex: Upload a CSV/XLSX/XML/TXT/JSON file (or paste delimited text), map it to a new or existing database table with column-type detection, null-value handling, and an Append/Replace update method, preview the result, then continue straight into the Create Application Wizard pre-populated with report/form/dashboard pages built on that table.
attributes: Upload a File tab (drag-drop or Choose File)
Copy and Paste tab (with sample datasets)
Load To: New Table (Primary Key strategy, column-type detection)
Column Mapping tab (Rows to Sample, Treat as Null)
workflow: Developer drops in a data file, maps its columns or accepts detected types, previews the parsed rows, loads it into a table, and lands in the Create Application Wizard with ready-made pages already built on that new table.
relevance: Upload-or-paste, map columns with type detection and null handling, preview, then auto-generate a working report or form is a strong pattern for a Paddock Developer import-a-CSV-of-results-or-schedule-data feature, minus the literal SQL table mechanics.
skip_for_web: New Table creation with Primary Keys (SYS_GUID/Identity Column), Parsing Schema and Table Owner are Oracle database provisioning details Paddock's data layer does not need to expose to an admin.

name: APEXlang (Application-as-Files for AI Agents)
apex: An open, human-readable application definition format that exports an app as a Git-friendly file tree (.apx definition files, Supporting Objects SQL, CSS/JS assets, static resources) instead of one large SQL script, explicitly designed so AI coding agents (Claude, Codex, etc.) can generate, read, and edit app code directly.
attributes: validated via apex validate in SQLcl
errors reference exact .apx file, line number, and component
warnings are informational, do not block import
workflow: Developer or their AI agent exports an app as APEXlang, edits the plain-text files directly in VS Code or similar, validates with apex validate before re-importing, fixing only reported errors.
relevance: This is precisely Paddock's own architecture already: content and config as Git-committed files an AI agent edits directly, not a monolithic DB blob. Confirms Paddock Developer should keep page/component definitions as reviewable files with a validator, not opaque DB rows.

name: Fusion Applications Integration (Create Fusion Integration Wizard)
apex: A specialized starter-app wizard that, given a pre-established Fusion Applications connection, auto-provisions a Remote Server, Web Credential, two REST Data Sources, six user-profile Application Items, an OAuth Authentication Scheme, and an example Authorization Scheme, all wired to a specific Oracle Fusion Applications instance.
attributes: auto-created REST Data Sources (HCM Self Details, Common Features User Roles)
workflow: Developer first runs a separate Database Tools wizard to connect APEX to a Fusion instance, then this wizard auto-generates a fully wired starter app against it.
relevance: A vertical integration exclusively for Oracle's own Fusion Applications ERP/HCM suite, requiring an Autonomous Database plus SQLNet to a Fusion tenancy; Paddock has no analogous enterprise system to integrate with.
skip_for_web: Entirely dependent on Oracle Fusion Applications, Autonomous Database, and SQLNet connectivity that do not exist in Paddock's stack.

name: JSON Application Blueprint (Wizard's Live State as Editable JSON)
apex: Every run of the Create Application Wizard maintains a live JSON document mirroring its current in-progress app definition; View Blueprint opens it in a code editor (Undo/Redo/Find/Replace) to hand-edit, and Apply Blueprint pushes edits back into the wizard's UI state; Load Previous Blueprint swaps in a prior generated app's JSON to iterate a design.
attributes: Load Blueprint page (load or delete a saved blueprint)
Load Previous Blueprint (reuse a prior app's definition)
workflow: Developer works the wizard UI normally, but drops into View Blueprint to bulk-edit or duplicate page JSON directly, faster than repeating Add Page many times, then Applies it back; or loads a previous app's blueprint to iterate a design before regenerating.
relevance: A two-way GUI-to-JSON editor with apply-back, used to bulk-duplicate near-identical pages faster than clicking through a wizard, is exactly the escape hatch Paddock Developer's own page or site builder should offer: edit the underlying JSON directly when the form UI is slower than editing structured data.

name: Copying an Application (Full Clone)
apex: Full clone of an app to a new Application ID and Name from the Application home page Tasks list, with an option to include or exclude Supporting Object Definitions (DB object, image, and seed-data scripts) in the copy.
workflow: Developer picks Copy this Application, names the clone and optionally sets its ID, decides whether to bring along supporting-object scripts, then confirms.
relevance: A full independent clone, distinct from a Working Copy which stays linked for merging, is a simple second option for Paddock Developer: duplicate this page or site with a new name when no future merge-back is intended.

name: Working Copies (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents topic for the Working Copy feature: what it is, how to create one, its menus and tasks, viewing/editing it, comparing it to Main or to other working copies, merging into Main, refreshing from Main, deleting it, and viewing its details.
attributes: Creating a Working Copy of an Application
About Working Copy Menus and Tasks
Viewing and Editing a Working Copy
Comparing Changes between a Working Copy and Main
Merging Changes from a Working Copy into Main
Refreshing a Working Copy with Changes from Main
View or Edit Working Copy Details
relevance: Stub page; the substantial concept and mechanics are covered in About Working Copies and its sibling pages.

name: About Working Copies (Diff/Merge Mechanics and Limits)
apex: A Working Copy is a linked, mergeable branch of an app: developers edit it in isolation, then a checksum-based diff (split YAML export of both apps) shows differences against Main, and a selective merge imports just the changed pages or shared components back, overwriting Main's version of anything touched. Refresh runs the same process in reverse. Several component types cannot be auto-merged and must be applied by hand.
attributes: Refresh (Main to Working Copy, reverse direction)
unsupported for auto-merge: Translations, Themes, Theme Templates, Supporting Objects, Application Properties, workspace-level components
cannot nest (no working copy of a working copy)
workflow: Developer branches a Working Copy, makes and tests changes in isolation, reviews a diff against Main, merges just the wanted changes back or refreshes the copy with Main's latest first, and manually reconciles anything on the unsupported-component list.
relevance: This is APEX's closest analog to git branch, diff, and merge, built into the GUI for non-technical builders; a Paddock Developer working-copy-with-selective-merge feature, with an explicit list of what cannot auto-merge, would let a content admin safely trial page changes without touching the live site.

name: Creating a Working Copy
apex: Application home page's Working Copy Tasks sidebar has a Create Working Copy wizard needing just a Name and Description; the new copy then displays its Working Copy Name next to the app name everywhere.
attributes: name badge shown next to app name
workflow: Developer names and describes the working copy, creates it, and immediately sees a visible badge distinguishing it from Main everywhere they navigate.
relevance: A persistent, always-visible badge naming which working copy versus Main you are editing is an important safety cue Paddock Developer must copy, so an admin editing a trial version never mistakes it for the live page.

name: Working Copy Menu (Context Switcher and Actions)
apex: A Working Copy: Name menu replaces the plain title wherever you are, on the Application home page menu bar and in the Page Designer toolbar, giving Switch to Main, a list of other Working Copies, Merge into Main (blocked if Main is locked by someone else), Refresh Working Copy, Compare Working Copy with Main, View Working Copy Details, and Delete Working Copy; Page Designer adds a page-scoped Compare Current Page with Main.
attributes: Merge into Main (disabled if Main locked)
sidebar shortcuts: Merge to Main/Refresh Working Copy/Compare Changes
Page Designer extra: Compare Current Page with Main
workflow: Developer works inside the working copy as normal, using the same-named menu to switch back to Main, merge, refresh, or compare at either the whole-app or single-page level without leaving the page they are on.
relevance: One context menu, present everywhere including inside the page editor, that always offers Switch to Main, Compare, Merge, Refresh, and Delete is the right always-available control surface for Paddock Developer's own working-copy mode, plus the page-scoped compare is a nice granularity to copy.

name: Viewing and Editing a Working Copy (App Builder Home Indicators)
apex: The App Builder home page itself shows a Working Copies count per app (a column in Report view, a number under the icon in Icon view) and a locked-padlock-with-user icon if a copy or Main is locked by someone else; selecting a copy from the sidebar opens it for editing exactly like a normal app.
attributes: Working Copies count (Icon view, under app name)
select a copy from the Working Copies sidebar list
workflow: Developer scans the app list, sees at a glance how many working copies an app has and whether any are locked, opens one, and edits it like any other app.
relevance: Surfacing a working-copy count and a lock indicator right on the main app list, before opening anything, is a good at-a-glance safety signal for Paddock Developer's own page or site list.

name: Comparing a Working Copy with Main (Diff Summary)
apex: Exports both the Working Copy and Main, compares them, and opens a summary dialog of what changed, was added, or is missing, with a further Compare Changes icon opening a detailed View Differences window; this comparison alone does not merge or refresh anything.
attributes: Compare Working Copy with Main (menu or sidebar)
Compare [Project Name] with Main summary dialog: Changed/Added/Missing
workflow: Developer opens the compare dialog to review a plain-language change summary before deciding whether to merge, refresh, or keep editing further.
relevance: A read-only, plain-language changed/added/missing summary before ever committing to a merge is the right safety step for Paddock Developer's working-copy feature: let an admin see exactly what a merge would do first.

name: Comparing a Page Across Multiple Working Copies
apex: Inside Page Designer, a View changes in other copies button, shown only if the current page was modified elsewhere, opens a Page Changes and Locks report of every copy (including Main) where that page differs or is locked, with a per-copy View Diff opening a side-by-side Viewing Page Differences dialog (Undo/Redo/Change/Next Change/Settings).
attributes: View changes in other copies button (Page Designer toolbar, conditional)
Page Changes and Locks dialog (report of copies)
workflow: Developer editing one page notices the conditional button, opens it to see every other working copy or Main that also touched this exact page, and steps through a diff to spot conflicting edits before merging.
relevance: Page-level cross-branch conflict detection, seeing every other copy that touched this specific page rather than only a whole-app diff, is an important safety feature for Paddock Developer if multiple admins can create working copies of the same page independently.

name: Merging a Working Copy into Main
apex: Opens the same changed/added/missing comparison as Compare, but lets you deselect individual rows to exclude specific changes from the merge, then Next reveals two safety options, Backup target app first and Delete Working Copy after merge, before Confirm Merge finalizes it.
attributes: Merge into Main (menu, sidebar, or Page Designer)
Merge dialog: Changed/Added/Missing rows, each deselectable
Compare Changes icon (view diff before merging)
workflow: Developer reviews the changed/added/missing list, deselects anything they do not want merged, opts to auto-backup Main first, optionally auto-deletes the working copy once merged, then confirms.
relevance: Row-level deselect-what-not-to-merge, plus a one-click auto-backup-before-merge safeguard and an auto-cleanup option, is exactly the granular, safe merge UX Paddock Developer's own working-copy-to-main flow should copy rather than an all-or-nothing publish.

name: Refreshing a Working Copy from Main
apex: The mirror of Merge: pulls Main's changes into the Working Copy instead, using the same changed/added/missing dialog with deselectable rows and a Backup target app first option, confirmed via Confirm Refresh.
attributes: Refresh Working Copy (menu, sidebar, or Page Designer)
workflow: Developer keeps a long-lived working copy current with Main's ongoing changes by refreshing periodically, rather than only merging one direction at the end.
relevance: Identical mechanic to Merging a Working Copy into Main, run in the opposite direction; the review, deselect, backup, confirm pattern is already credited there.

name: Deleting a Working Copy
apex: A one-step confirm dialog, Delete Working Copy, reached from the Working Copy: Name menu; removes the copy entirely.
workflow: Developer abandons a working copy they no longer need via the menu and one confirmation click.
relevance: A single-step delete confirmation with no soft-delete or recovery, weaker than the issue tracker's own soft-delete pattern already credited as worth copying; nothing new here.

name: Viewing or Editing Working Copy Details
apex: A small dialog to rename or re-describe an existing Working Copy after creation, saved via Apply Changes.
workflow: Developer opens Working Copy Details later to correct or clarify the name or description originally set at creation.
relevance: Trivial rename/re-describe dialog; no new pattern beyond standard metadata editing.

name: Creating Applications for Mobile Devices (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents topic framing mobile support as two things: the Universal Theme's built-in responsive design, no separate mobile UI needed, and, optionally, Progressive Web App packaging.
relevance: Confirms APEX's mobile strategy is one responsive theme, not a separate mobile codebase, which validates Paddock's own responsive-web-first approach and needs no distinct mobile mode in Paddock Developer.

name: Advantages of the Universal Theme (Design Philosophy)
apex: The theme's three pitched advantages: automatic Responsive Design across screen sizes (vector graphics, CSS3), a Versatile UI covering practically any business-app need, and Easy Customization (Theme Roller plus Template Options) letting non-experts fully restyle an app without HTML, CSS, or JavaScript knowledge.
attributes: Easy Customization (Theme Roller + Template Options, no code required)
workflow: Developer relies on one theme for every screen size and reaches for Theme Roller or Template Options instead of hand-written CSS whenever the brand needs adjusting.
relevance: This is Paddock Developer's own mission statement in miniature: one responsive component system, broad enough for any page, restylable by a non-technical admin without touching code, worth stating explicitly as a design principle.
skip_for_web: The jQuery-Mobile-to-Universal-Theme migration note is legacy-specific to old APEX apps; Paddock has no jQuery Mobile history to migrate away from.
